candidate: C3_flow = kappa^2 eta q - (1-a) kappa from dp = kappa u - (1-a) x_lag and u = (1-eta) u_lag + eta q x_lag, x = log price minus EMA(30 minutes), u = signed flow over the symbol's median absolute training-minute flow
data: Alpaca market-data API, consolidated (SIP) trades, regular session 09:30-16:00 ET on full trading days; minute bars of last trade price, tick-rule signed dollar flow, dollar volume; a day is valid if >= 80% of minutes have a trade
inclusion: a symbol enters if it has >= 30 valid training days and >= 25 valid test days; tickers listed in 2026 only (delisted stocks are not in the asset list), which we report as a survivorship limitation
inference: Clark-West (Newey-West 6 lags); 2,000 date-block bootstrap draws; secondary Holm-adjusted

primary.success: Clark-West one-sided p < 0.05 AND 95% date-block bootstrap CI of dR2 above 0

question: Regulated market: in thin US common stocks, does the depth-free amplification margin C3_flow forecast the next hour's maximum adverse excursion beyond volatility forecasts and price impact?
relation: Fifth venue-level test of the thin-book result; first in a regulated market
runs: A5 is run once; every run is counted in prereg/test_set_unlocks_p14.json
secondary: thin: MAE | S60 (summed |response| of the depth-free model, 60 minutes)
mid control: MAE | C3_flow (predicted: little or no effect)
unit: symbol x forecast time t in {120, 180, 240, 300} minutes after the open; features from minutes [t-120, t); outcome MAE over (t, t+60] in basis points
